'''''Iris foetidissima''''', the '''stinking iris''',<ref name=Fitter>Richard Fitter, Alastair Fitter and Marjorie Blamey {{google books|R9OEkTareSoC&|Wild Flowers of Britain and Northern Europe (1996)|page=284}}</ref> '''gladdon''', '''Gladwin iris''', '''roast-beef plant''', or '''stinking gladwin''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[family (botany)|family]] Iridaceae, found in open woodland, hedgebanks and on sea-cliffs.

Its natural range is Western Europe, including England (south of [[Durham, England|Durham]]) and also Ireland, and from France south and east to N. Africa, Italy and Greece.<ref>[[Plants For A Future]]: [http://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Iris+foetidissima ''Iris foetidissima'']</ref> 
[[Image:Iris foetidisima graines.jpg|thumb|Seeds]]

It is one of two iris species native to Britain, the other being the yellow iris (''[[Iris pseudacorus]]'').

It has tufts of dark green leaves.<ref name=Fitter/> Its flowers are usually of a dull, leaden-blue colour, or dull buff-yellow tinged with blue. The petals have delicate veining. It blooms between June and July, but the flowers only last a day or so.<ref name="Cuttle"/>
The green seed capsules, which remain attached to the plant throughout the winter, are {{convert|5|-|8|cm|0|abbr=on}} long; and the seeds are scarlet.

It is known as "stinking" because some people find the smell of its leaves unpleasant when crushed or bruised,<ref name=Fitter/> an odour that has been described as "beefy". Its common names of 'gladdon' and 'gladwyn' or 'gladwin', are in reference to an old word for a sword (Latin {{Lang|la|gladius}}) due to the shape of the iris's leaves.<ref name="Cuttle">{{cite book |last1=Spencer-Jones |first1=Rae |last2=Cuttle |first2=Sarah |title=Wild Flowers of Britain and Ireland |date=2005 |publisher=Kyle Cathie Limited |location=London |isbn=9781856265034 |page=88}}</ref>

This plant is cultivated in gardens in the [[Temperateness|temperate]] zones. Both the species<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Iris foetidissima''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/9250/Iris-foetidissima/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=2020-09-16}}</ref> and its [[cultivar]] 'Variegata'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Iris foetidissima'' 'Variegata'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/93688/Iris-foetidissima-Variegata-(v)/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=2020-09-16}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 53 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 13 March 2018}}</ref>
